key_insight: The paper shows that designing shallow quantum circuits for binary polynomial optimization can be formulated as a classical binary linear problem, enabling much shorter circuits than standard approaches.
engineering_relevance: This matters for near-term quantum hardware because reducing circuit depth can improve feasibility for higher-degree optimization models without requiring unavailable multi-qubit gates.
method: Formulate shallow circuit design as a binary linear optimization problem.
Prove NP-completeness for a variant of the circuit-design problem.
Introduce Tempura, a scalable heuristic, plus faster approximate binary linear formulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the proposed algorithms produce far shorter circuits than state-of-the-art methods while Tempura remains mostly comparable in runtime.
watch_item: The faster formulations trade optimality for computational feasibility, so solution quality may depend on the instance and approximation level.
paper_title: Circuit Design Problems in Binary Polynomial Quantum Optimization
